summary: Recapture the website gallery from a locally deployed Controller and extend it with the managed virtual-machine views (pool VM list, VM details, Create VM review) so the gallery shows the VM work added since 9 September. API impact: existing contract; the capture harness exercises the shipped session, enrollment, mTLS reporting, storage/network/media registration and VM creation contracts without changing them.

guide.reason: The gallery a reader reaches from the website now contains three additional virtual-machine views, so the documented walkthrough names what is shown.

api.reason: Screenshot capture and static website content only. The harness calls the existing session, site, enrollment-token, agent enroll/report, storage, network, media and VM creation contracts as an ordinary client; no contract, authorization, validation or error behavior changes, so no reference update is required.

state.reason: Website images, website source and disposable capture tooling only. The demo Controller state lives in a temporary directory that is deleted when the harness exits; no Nex Controller or Nex Core durable state is added or changed.

verification.method: Rebuilt web/dist with npm run typecheck clean. Ran tests/integration/website_controller_captures.py against a real Controller binary with a simulated enrolled host: all five checks passed, including the privacy guard rejecting the original workstation label. All seven captures inspected individually. Built the website (svelte-check 0 errors, 0 warnings), served the build on a local listener and ran tests/integration/website_browser.py: all twelve groups passed at 1440px, 768px and 360px and with JavaScript disabled; the rendered gallery page was inspected. Host inventory and VMs are a declared simulation, so this is evidence of Controller UI rendering, not of libvirt or guest behavior. Not published: no deployed-site evidence is claimed.
